limitPokemonCheckBox:
Select this to allow yourself to limit the Pokemon used by the randomization.
If this box isn't checked all Pokemon will be allowed.
raceModeCheckBox:
Select this to enable certain things which are useful for a speedrun race of the ROM you create.
The ability to save a log file will be disabled, and a check value will be generated.
You can send this value around with the preset file to ensure that everyone has the same ROM to race with.
noIrregularAltFormesCheckBox:
Bans "irregular" alternate formes from the Pokemon pool when "Allow Alternate Formes" is selected for Wild Pokemon, Trainer Pokemon, Evolutions, etc.
Irregular formes are those that normally cannot exist outside of battle (such as Mega Evolutions and other in-battle transformations like Darmanitan-Z, Zygarde-C, etc),
as well as the "Fusion" Pokemon (Kyurem-B/W and Necrozma-DM/DW).
These alternate formes still exist and will get randomized base stats, abilities and so on (according to your settings),
but they can only be accessed through their regular means (such as by Mega Evolving or transforming because of an Ability).
noPrematureEvosCheckbox:
If this is checked, any randomly chosen Pokemon will not be prematurely evolved, i.e., only Pokemon that cannot evolve at the given level are chosen.
For any Pokemon that does not evolve by level up, its Estimated Evolution Level is used which is deduced from all level up evolutions.
Currently affects:
• Trainer Pokemon (note that the evolution levels there are affected by the percentage slider below 'Trainers Evolve their Pokemon') and
• Wild Pokemon, if neither 'Same Evolution Stage' nor 'Keep Relations' is selected.
noRandomIntroMonCheckBox:
If checked, the Pokemon sent out by the professor in the intro, will not be randomized.
In HGSS, the intro mon is Ethan's/Lyra's Marill.
The intro mon is randomized by default, because it is a good way of telling whether the Randomizer has been applied.
loadSettingsButton:
Clicking this button allows you to load predefined settings from a file.
If the file was created with a game which has less randomization options
than the one you are randomizing now, those options will be set to "Unchanged"/Off.
If you load from a newer game, everything that isn't supported will be ignored.
saveSettingsButton:
Clicking this will allow you to save the current randomization settings as a file.
You can then load these settings when you are randomizing any ROM.
The way in which ROMs with more or less features than the current one
 are handled is described when you hover over the "Load Settings" button.
pbsUnchangedRadioButton: Don't change Pokemon stats from the base at all.
pbsShuffleRadioButton:
Shuffle each Pokemon's stats.
For example, its base Attack may be swapped with its base Special Attack, etc.
This does not make any Pokemon stronger or weaker.
pbsRandomRadioButton:
Randomizes each Pokemon's stats, as long as they fall within the original base stat total.
This could make Pokemon stronger or weaker if they get unlucky or lucky rolls on stats they need.
Evolutions of a Pokemon will be treated separately from that Pokemon unless you check Follow Evolutions.
pbsLegendariesSlowRadioButton: All legendaries get the "Slow" EXP Curve.
pbsStrongLegendariesSlowRadioButton:
Strong legendaries get the "Slow" EXP Curve.
This includes all legendaries with >600 BST.
pbsAllMediumFastRadioButton: All Pokemon get the selected EXP Curve.
pbsStandardizeEXPCurvesCheckBox:
When this is selected, every Pokemon's EXP curve will be changed to the selected EXP curve below,
except for the Pokemon forced to use the "Slow" EXP curve, chosen with the settings to the right.
This will cause Pokemon to be better or worse based more on their stats/moves/type rather than the difficulty of leveling them;
it will also allow for more potential evolutions if you randomize evolutions, since a Pokemon only can evolve into a Pokemon with the same EXP curve.
If you're not sure which EXP Curve to pick, Medium Fast and Medium Slow are generally good curves (most Pokemon use these in the regular games).
pbsFollowEvolutionsCheckBox:
When this is selected and base stats are shuffled or randomized, evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit from their base form's rolls.
Shuffle: The same new ordering of stats will be used.
Randomized: The evolution will have the same proportion of stats as the base form.
pbsUpdateBaseStatsCheckBox:
Select this to update the base stats of Pokemon in the loaded game to their values in the generation chosen to the right.
This does NOT:
* Add any new Pokemon to the game
* Split Special Attack and Special Defense in Gen 1.
ptUnchangedRadioButton: Don't change Pokemon types at all.
ptRandomFollowEvolutionsRadioButton:
Randomize the types of each Pokemon, but make most evolutions copy the base Pokemon (except perhaps adding an extra secondary type).
Evolutions that don't copy types are the Eeveelutions, among others.
ptRandomCompletelyRadioButton:
Randomize Pokemon types completely.
Evolutions of a Pokemon are completely separate from that Pokemon, so the type of a Pokemon will likely completely change every evolution.
paUnchangedRadioButton: Don't change Pokemon abilities from the base at all.
paRandomRadioButton:
Give each Pokemon new abilities.
Each Pokemon will have a base ability, and a 50% chance of having a 2nd ability different from the first.
(50% of the species will have this ability if it is made).
In Generation 5 games, each Pokemon will also receive a new random "Dream World" ability.
Pokemon such as Shedinja which have Wonder Guard as their ability will keep it to maintain balance.
paAllowWonderGuardCheckBox:
If this is checked, Wonder Guard will be able to be chosen as any Pokemon's ability.
This can lead to some very overpowered/broken Pokemon.
USE WITH CAUTION!
paFollowEvolutionsCheckBox: When this is selected and abilities are randomized, non-split evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit that Pokemon's random abilities.
paTrappingAbilitiesCheckBox:
When abilities are randomized, ban abilities that can prevent the opponent from fleeing/switching out from being selected.
This bans Arena Trap, Magnet Pull and Shadow Tag.
Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.
Pokemon that have a trapping ability to begin with will still have their abilities randomized, unlike how Wonder Guard is treated.
paNegativeAbilitiesCheckBox:
When abilities are randomized, ban abilities that are purely negative in nature from being chosen.
This bans Defeatist, Slow Start, Truant, Klutz, Stall.
Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.
Pokemon that have a negative ability to begin with will still have their abilities randomized, unlike how Wonder Guard is treated.
paBadAbilitiesCheckBox:
When abilities are randomized, ban bad abilities.
This bans Minus, Plus, Anticipation, Forewarn, Frisk, Honey Gather, Aura Break, Receiver, Power of Alchemy.
If "Double Battle Mode" for Trainers is not selected, it also bans Friend Guard, Healer, Telepathy, Symbiosis, Battery.
Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.
paEnsureTwoAbilitiesCheckbox: When abilities are randomized, ensure each Pokemon has two abilities.
peRandomRadioButton:
Randomize which species each Pokemon evolves into.
Evolutions will be mostly unrestricted unless you check some boxes to the right, but the EXP curves of the Pokemon must match.
If the randomizer has trouble randomizing Evolutions, "Standardize EXP Curves" might help.
peRandomEveryLevelRadioButton:
Randomize which species each Pokemon evolves into while forcing them to evolve every single level.
All existing evolutions for a given Pokemon will be removed and replaced with a single Level 1 evolution.
Evolutions will be mostly unrestricted unless you check some boxes to the right, but the EXP curves of the Pokemon must match.
If the randomizer has trouble randomizing Evolutions, "Standardize EXP Curves" might help.
Evolution "loops" are expected and intended with this setting.
peSimilarStrengthCheckBox:
When this is checked, random evolutions will prefer Pokemon with a similar BST to the original evolution target.
Has less precedence than all other modifiers below, so it may not always be strictly enforced.
peSameTypingCheckBox: When selected, randomized evolutions will share at least one type between the source and target.
peLimitEvolutionsToThreeCheckBox: When selected, there will not be any evolution chains created that are longer than three stages.
peForceChangeCheckBox: When selected, every evolution of a Pokemon will be randomized to something different than what it was originally.
peChangeImpossibleEvosCheckBox:
If this is checked, every evolution that isn't possible to do without trading in the current game will be changed.
Takes effect regardless of whether evolutions are randomized or not.
Some of the types that will be changed are:
• "Normal" trade evolutions
• Trade evolutions with another condition, such as held item or Pokemon traded for
• Day/night evolutions if there isn't day/night in the game
• Contest-stat evolutions if there aren't contests in the game
• Location-based evolutions, if those locations don't exist in the game
• Move-based evolutions, only if you randomize movesets
peUseEstimatedInsteadOfHardcodedLevelsCh:
If this is checked, evolutions that were changed to become level-up evolutions via the 'Change Impossible Evolutions' or the 'Make Evolutions Easier' option 
will use evolution levels estimated from all other evolution levels in the current game instead of a pre-set evolution level.
peMakeEvolutionsEasierCheckBox:
If this is checked, Pokemon that evolve at a very high level will evolve at lower levels to make them more viable for shorter playthroughs.
Specifically, every Pokemon will evolve to its final stage by the level selected below, and three-stage evolutions will reach their middle stage by no later than 75% of the level selected below.
(If the maximum value of the slider below is selected, evolutions levels will not be changed but the following improvements will still apply.)
Additionally, Pokemon that normally evolve by having another specific Pokemon in the party will instead evolve at level 35.
Lastly, Pokemon that evolve via friendship will evolve at 160 happiness (down from 220), similar to how it works in the Switch Pokemon games.
Takes effect regardless of whether evolutions are randomized or not.
peMakeEvolutionsEasierLvlSlider:
Use this slider to select the level by which every Pokemon shall be evolved to its final stage if 'Make Evolutions Easier' is checked above.
If the maximum value of this slider is selected, evolution levels will not be changed (other evolution improvements of 'Make Evolutions Easier' still apply).
peRemoveTimeBasedEvolutions:
If this is checked, evolutions that require a certain time of day will now be possible regardless of the in-game time.
Split time-based evolutions (like Eevee => Espeon/Umbreon and Rockruff => Lycanroc) will be changed to stone evolutions instead.
peAdjustLevelsCheckBox:
If this is checked, level-up evolutions will have their levels algorithmically adjusted,
to better fit the Pokemon before and after evolution.
E.g., if a Pokemon evolves into Dragonite, it will do so at a high level.
This option also affects estimated evo levels, used elsewhere in the Randomizer
for Pokemon that do not evolve via level-up.
spCustomRadioButton: Lets you pick the 3 starter pokemon you want to use, or "Random" at the top of the selector.
spRandomCompletelyRadioButton: Picks 3 random starter Pokemon to be used.
spRandomTwoEvosRadioButton:
Picks 3 random starter Pokemon to be used.
These Pokemon must have 2 evolution stages, e.g. be like the starters in the real games.
spRandomizeStarterHeldItemsCheckBox:
Checking this will randomize the items held by the starters where possible.
In Generation 2 games, each starter will get an individual random item.
In Generation 3 games, all the starters will get the same random item.
spBanBadItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for starter Pokemon, such as berries and mail.
stpSwapLegendariesSwapStandardsRadioButt:
Selecting this will replace every static Pokemon encounter, gift or purchase with another random one.
In this particular mode, legendary pokemon will always be swapped for other legendaries.
Also, normal non-legendary Pokemon will only be swapped for other non-legendaries.
In games where Ultra Beasts appear, they will be swapped out for other Ultra Beasts.
stpRandomCompletelyRadioButton:
Selecting this will replace every static Pokemon encounter, gift or purchase with another random one.
In this particular mode, any Pokemon can replace any other Pokemon, so you could get a Mew in the Game Corner.
Or fight Magikarp instead of Mewtwo...
stpRandomSimilarStrengthRadioButton: Selecting this will replace every static Pokemon encounter with a Pokemon of similar strength.
stpLimitMainGameLegendariesCheckBox:
Selecting this will prevent main-game Legendary Pokemon from being replaced by Pokemon with higher base stat totals.
This only applies to main-game Legendary Pokemon that are catchable and that are directly in your way during the main game, so some Pokemon
like Kyurem-B/Kyurem-W in BW2 (not catchable) and Rayquaza in Emerald (have to go out of your way to catch) are not included.
stpRandomize600BSTCheckBox: Selecting this will enforce pure random on all static Pokemon with 600+ BST.
igtRandomizeGivenPokemonOnlyRadioButton:
Selecting this will randomize the Pokemon you receive from each in-game trade,
but the Pokemon requested by the NPC in exchange will remain the same.
igtRandomizeBothRequestedGivenRadioButto: Selecting this will replace both the Pokemon you receive from an in-game trade and the Pokemon required to do the trade.
igtRandomizeNicknamesCheckBox:
Check this to randomize the nicknames of the Pokemon you receive.
The nicknames will be chosen from a predefined list.
If there are no more usable nicknames the original nicknames will be kept for the rest of the trades.
igtRandomizeOTsCheckBox:
Check this to randomize the Original Trainer (ID & name) of the Pokemon you receive from trades.
The names will be chosen from the same list as trainer names,
with names that are too long to be OT names excluded.
igtRandomizeIVsCheckBox:
Check this to randomize the IVs of the Pokemon you receive from ingame trades.
In most games these Pokemon have set IVs, so clicking this randomizes those set IVs.
igtRandomizeItemsCheckBox:
Check this to give each Pokemon you receive from an ingame trade a random held item.
This includes trades that do not normally have a held item on the Pokemon.
mdRandomizeMovePowerCheckBox:
Randomize the power of normal damaging moves.
Moves will get a new random power generally between 20 and 150 inclusive, with a very small chance of higher values appearing.
Non-damaging moves and moves with variable power will be unaffected.
NOTE: There is no way to see the updated power of moves in-game in Gen 1!
mdRandomizeMoveAccuracyCheckBox:
Randomize the accuracy of most moves.
Some restrictions are enforced to reduce the chances of situations like 100% accurate OHKO moves happening.
Sure-hit moves are not changed.
NOTE: There is no way to see the updated accuracy of moves in-game in Gen 1!
mdRandomizeMovePPCheckBox:
Randomize the PP of each move.
The maximum PP of each move (before PP Ups) will be randomized to a multiple of 5 between 5 and 40 inclusive.
mdRandomizeMoveTypesCheckBox:
Randomize the type of most moves.
The type of each move other than Struggle and ???-type moves will be re-rolled randomly.
This has no real effect on self-status moves, and may have odd side-effects in Gen 1.
mdRandomizeMoveNamesCheckBox:
Randomize names of moves.
The name chosen will be based off the Type of the move.
If Randomized Move Types are on, then the name will be based on the randomized type.
NOTE: This feature is only available for Gen 3+ English-language games.
mdRandomizeMoveCategoryCheckBox:
Randomize the category of damaging moves between Physical and Special.
This does not affect status moves.
NOTE: This feature is not available for Gen 1-3 games. This randomizer does NOT add the Physical/Special split to games that don't have it!
mdUpdateMovesCheckBox:
If this is checked, moves will be updated to their stats (power, accuracy, etc) in the generation chosen to the right where possible.
This does NOT add the Fairy type! Moves that were changed to Fairy type will keep their Gen 5 types.
Note that this only affects move stats, not any secondary effects that may have been added.
mdLegacyCheckBox:
Instead of updating moves to their Gen 6 stats, update them to their Gen 5 stats instead.
This is intended for people who used the "Update Moves" function in old randomizers but don't like the new changes.
This is available for every game except Gen 5 games where it would be pointless.
pmsUnchangedRadioButton: Don't change Pokemon movesets at all.
pmsRandomPreferringSameTypeRadioButton:
Randomize Pokemon movesets, preferring moves that are of the type (or one of the types) of the Pokemon.
Each Pokemon will get at least one reasonably accurate damaging move to begin with.
pmsRandomCompletelyRadioButton:
Randomize Pokemon movesets, completely ignoring the type of the move and the Pokemon.
Each Pokemon will get at least one reasonably accurate damaging move to begin with.
pmsMetronomeOnlyModeRadioButton:
Where possible, every Pokémon in the entire game will have Metronome as its only move,
 with the PP boosted to 40 to make it possible to complete fights without always using Struggle.
Does not currently apply to non-standard battles such as the Battle Tower/Frontier or the PWT.
pmsGuaranteedLevel1MovesCheckBox:
Check this to make sure every Pokemon gets a guaranteed amount of moves at level 1, instead of them keeping their original move count.
Set amount of guaranteed moves with the slider to the right.
Setting this to 4 ensures that every Pokemon you catch will have a full moveset.
pmsReorderDamagingMovesCheckBox:
Reorders the randomized movesets so that less powerful damaging moves are learnt before those with high power.
The positions of non-damaging moves will not change.
pmsNoGameBreakingMovesCheckBox:
Checking this checkbox will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized movesets.
In first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.
In second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).
pmsForceGoodDamagingCheckBox:
Selecting this option will allow you to use the slider below to select a proportion of the randomized movesets to be forced to be good damaging moves.
Note that other moves can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
pmsGuaranteedLevel1MovesSlider: Set amount of guaranteed moves at level 1. Applies to all Pokemon.
pmsForceGoodDamagingSpinSlider:
Use this slider to select the probability of good damaging moves for the option above.
Note that other moves can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
tpMain0Unchanged:
Don't change original trainer Pokemon at all.
If additional Pokemon are added to a trainer, they will be chosen according to the option "Keep Type Themed Trainers' Themes".
tpUnchangedRadioButton: Don't change trainer Pokemon at all.
tpMain2RandomEvenDistribution:
For all trainers in the game (main-game and post-game), attempt to distribute Pokemon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokemon from appearing too often.
tpRandomEvenDistributionRadioButton:
For all trainers in the game (main-game and post-game), attempt to distribute Pokemon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokemon from appearing too often.
tpMain3RandomEvenDistributionMainGame:
For all trainers in the game (main-game trainers only), attempt to distribute Pokemon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokemon from appearing too often.
Balancing among main game trainers causes evenness with a standard playthrough, and ignores post-game trainers (they are simply random).
This setting is for Gen 5 only.
tpRandomEvenDistributionMainRadioButton:
For all trainers in the game (main-game trainers only), attempt to distribute Pokemon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokemon from appearing too often.
Balancing among main game trainers causes evenness with a standard playthrough, and ignores post-game trainers (they are simply random).
This setting is for Gen 5 only.
tpMain4TypeThemed:
Pick a type for each trainer and give them random Pokemon in that type.
Certain groups of trainers, such as the trainers in each gym, will all be given the same (random) type.
tpTypeThemedRadioButton:
Pick a type for each trainer and give them random Pokemon in that type.
Certain groups of trainers, such as the trainers in each gym, will all be given the same (random) type.
tpMain5TypeThemedEliteFourGyms:
Pick a type for each trainer and give them random Pokemon in that type.
Certain groups of trainers, such as the trainers in each gym, will all be given the same (random) type.
Only applies to Elite Four and Gym Trainers/Leaders.
tpMain6KeepThemed:
If a trainer originally had only Pokemon of a certain type, randomly chooses new pokemon of that type.
(Trainers with only one Pokemon are considered themed.)
Gym trainers and Elite Four/Champions will be forced to their "official" type theme, even if they did not originally follow it.
All other trainers will have random Pokemon.
tpMain7KeepThemed:
If a trainer originally had only Pokemon of a certain type, randomly chooses new pokemon of that type.
Gym trainers and Elite Four/Champions will be forced to their "official" type theme, even if they did not originally follow it.
Otherwise, for each Pokemon, replaces it with a Pokemon that shares its primary type.
For example, a Grass-Poison type might be replaced with a pure Grass type, a Grass-Psychic type, or a Bug-Grass type.
tpRivalCarriesStarterCheckBox:
If this is selected, the rival will have their starter in every team they battle you with, evolved if it is far enough through.
The rest of their team will be chosen in the same way as every other trainer.
tpSimilarStrengthCheckBox:
If this is checked, the random Pokemon that replaces each Pokemon will be of similar power to the original.
However, preserving other rules such as type theming or avoiding duplicates has precedence over this, so weaker or stronger Pokemon will be chosen if there are no other Pokemon available.
tpAvoidDuplicatesCheckBox:
If this is checked, any randomly chosen Pokemon for a given trainer will be different from the other Pokemon of the trainer.
However, if other rules restrict the set of allowed Pokemon too much, duplicates are possible.
tpWeightTypesCheckBox:
If this is checked, the number of trainers with each type will roughly match up to the number of Pokemon with that type.
This should reduce repetition of Pokemon, but may lead to a lot of trainers with the same type in a row.
tpNoEarlyWonderGuardCheckBox:
Pokemon such as Shedinja, with the ability "Wonder Guard", are a pain to run into early on when you can't damage them.
Selecting this option will make sure that no trainers are given these Pokemon under level 20.
By the time you are fighting level 20 trainers you can reasonably be expected to have a counter for each type.
tpRandomizeTrainerNamesCheckBox:
Check this to randomize trainers' names when you fight them.
For RBY, this only includes the Gym Leaders and Elite 4, as no-one else has names.
For every other game this will replace the names of each individual trainer.
tpRandomizeTrainerClassNamesCheckBox: Check this to randomize the class names to new names (e.g. "Youngster" could become "Misfit").
tpTrainersEvolveTheirPokemonCheckbox:
Checking this will guarantee that any trainer Pokemon is evolved as far as possible at its level.
For any Pokemon that does not evolve by level up, its Estimated Evolution Level is used which is deduced from all level up evolutions.
tpPercentageEvolutionLevelModifierSpinSl:
Use this slider to select the percentage to scale trainer Pokemon evolution levels by.
Negative percentages (-100 to 0) will decrease trainer Pokemon evolution levels, making battles harder.
Positive percentages will increase trainer Pokemon evolution levels, making battles easier.
Estimated Evolution Levels of Pokemon are scaled by the value selected as well.
Note that the minimal possible level is 1 and the maximal possible level is 100.
tpCalculatedFullyEvolvedLvlLabel:
Displays the level at which all trainer Pokemon will be fully evolved if 'Trainers Evolve their Pokemon' is selected.
 The displayed level will change based on the percentage chosen for scaling trainer Pokemon evolution levels above as well as the level chosen for 'Make Evolutions Easier' if that option is selected.
tpPercentageLevelModifierSpinSlider:
Use this slider to select the percentage to change trainer Pokemon levels by.
Negative percentages (-100 to 0) will decrease levels, and positive percentages will increase them.
Note that the minimal possible level is 1 and the maximal possible level is 100.
tpPercentageLevelModifierCheckBox: Checking this will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every enemy trainer Pokemon in the game.
tpAllowAlternateFormesCheckBox:
Allow trainers to have alternate formes of Pokemon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys.
Note that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.
wpRandomizeWildPokemonCheckBox: Whether to randomize wild Pokemon encounters.
wpZoneNoneRadioButton:
Place the maximum possible amount of different Pokemon encounters into each area.
This amount varies by game and area (higher in later generations), but is typically in the range 5-10 per encounter type.
wpZoneEncounterSetRadioButton:
Each Pokemon in a given encounter set will be replaced by another Pokemon in every slot it appears in.
 This will make each set have a handful of random Pokemon.
 Each "set" is a smaller chunk of encounter data, e.g. different floors of the same dungeon or fishing/surfing on the same route,
 or encounters for morning/day/night or seasons if "Use Time Based Encounters" is selected, count as separate sets.
 Using this option they will be randomized separately.
 Compare to "1 Per Location".
wpZoneMapRadioButton:
On each map, each Pokemon will be replaced by exactly one new Pokemon.
A map is the portion of a single named area that is loaded at one time, such as a route, a single floor of a cave or tower, etc.
Compare to "1 Per Location".
In some games, there are encounter sets that are shared between multiple maps. These will be considered their own maps, but any that are
 shared between the same set of maps will be grouped into a single pseudo-map.
wpZoneLocationRadioButton:
Each Pokemon in a given location will be replaced by another Pokemon in every slot it appears in.
 This will make each location have a handful of random Pokemon.
 A location is essentially a named place on the town map, e.g. different floors of the same dungeon
 or fishing/surfing on the same route may count as separate maps or encounter sets, but they still fall under the same location.
 Using this option they will be randomized together.
 Compare to "1 Per Encounter Set" or "1 Per Map".
 Due to technical limitations, some locations may be unintuitive:
 In Gen 1, the old rod and good rod each constitute their own location.
 In Gen 1, except Yellow, super rod encounters may be shared by multiple routes/towns/dungeons and are categorized into "groups" by the game.
 Each of these "groups" is counted as a location. 
 In Gen 2, fishing and headbutt encounters may be shared by multiple routes/towns/dungeons and are categorized into "groups" by the game. Each of these "groups" is counted as a location.
wpZoneGlobalRadioButton: Every place a certain Pokemon appears in, it will be replaced by another set Pokemon.
wpERBasicOnlyRadioButton:
If selected, only Pokemon which no Pokemon can evolve into will be selected.
If used with "Keep Relations", each evolutionary family chosen will begin with one such Pokemon.
wpERSameEvolutionStageRadioButton:
If selected, each randomly-chosen Pokemon will have the same evolutionary stage as the Pokemon it replaced,
as measured from the first Pokemon in the evolutionary family.
For example, Tauros, Krabby, and Pichu would all be the same stage, but Pikachu would not(except in Generation 1).
wpERNoneRadioButton: Don't apply any evolutionary stage restriction.
wpKeepEvolutionsCheckBox:
If multiple Pokemon related by evolution appear in the same zone, their replacements will also be related in the same way.
A "zone" is the area in which a Pokemon will be replaced by the same Pokemon, as determined by the option chosen.
(Branched families may be merged into a single line.)
Only checks most other restrictions (e.g. similar strength, types) against a single Pokemon in the line, so may sometimes have odd results.
wpSplitByEncounterTypesCheckBox:
Split the game, map, or location by encounter types, such as walking, Surfing, fishing, and Rock Smash.
This means that (for example) a Tentacool encountered while Surfing will be replaced with a different Pokemon than a Tentacool encountered while fishing.
wpSimilarStrengthCheckBox:
If this is checked, the random Pokemon that replaces each Pokemon will be of similar power to the original.
However, preserving other rules such as 1-1 maps, catch 'em all, or type restrictions has precedence over this, so weaker or stronger Pokemon will be chosen if there are no other Pokemon available.
wpCatchEmAllModeCheckBox:
If this is turned on, every random Pokemon chosen to replace an encounter will be one that hasn't been chosen before.
 Once every Pokemon has been chosen once, any Pokemon may be chosen (respecting other options).
 When used with other less restrictive options, this should make sure that every Pokemon is catchable somewhere.
 More restrictive other options may make it logically impossible to place all Pokemon, in which case as many Pokemon as possible will be placed.
 E.g. with "No Legendaries" or Generation restrictions ("Limit Pokemon") it won't be able to place those Pokemon,
 and "Keep Primary Type" will make it impossible to place all Dragon types in most games, as there are too few wild Dragon types to replace.
wpUseTimeBasedEncountersCheckBox:
This affects games that have either seasons or morning/day/night encounter sets.
If this is checked, each of these sets will be treated as a separate "area".
So you will have to visit each place in morning/day/night, or in each season, to collect the Pokemon.
If this isn't checked, each of morning/day/night and all seasons will use the same encounter data.
wpSetMinimumCatchRateCheckBox:
If this is selected, every Pokemon in the game with a catch rate below a certain level will have its catch rate increased.
The exact minimum catch rate level can be set using the slider to the right.
The percentages below assume a normal Poke Ball is used while the wild Pokemon is at full health with no status condition.
Level 1: "Normal" minimum catch rate. ~10% (Gens 1-4)/~18% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~5% (Gens 1-4)/~10% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 2: "Buffed" minimum catch rate. ~17% (Gens 1-4)/~26% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~9% (Gens 1-4)/~16% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 3: "Super" minimum catch rate. ~27% (Gens 1-4)/~37% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~14% (Gens 1-4)/~22% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 4: "Ultra" minimum catch rate. ~34% (Gens 1-4)/~44% (Gens 5+) chance for all Pokemon. 
Level 5: Guaranteed catches (every Pokemon is guaranteed to be caught, so long as they are catchable in the first place).
wpRandomizeHeldItemsCheckBox:
Checking this will randomize the items held by Pokemon in the wild, including whether they can have one at all or not.
In some cases, these item definitions will also apply to static encounters with legendaries and the like.
wpBanBadItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for wild Pokemon, such as berries and mail.
wpBalanceShakingGrassPokemonCheckBox:
Checking this sets an upper limit for the base stat total of wild Pokemon based on their level when using the "Similar Strength" setting.
This limit is high enough that it only changes abnormally strong Pokemon for the level (e.g. Geodude below level 5, Audino below level 20).
The level used for this calculation is the lowest level encounter with this Pokemon in the same-replacement zone.
wpPercentageLevelModifierCheckBox: Checking this will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every wild Pokemon in the game.
wpPercentageLevelModifierSpinSlider:
Use this slider to select the percentage to change wild Pokemon levels by.
Negative percentages (-100 to 0) will decrease levels, and positive percentages will increase them.
Note that the minimal possible level is 1 and the maximal possible level is 100.
wpSetMinimumCatchRateSlider:
If Minimum Catch Rate is selected, allows you to set the level used. The percentages below assume a normal Poke Ball at full health.
Level 1: "Normal" minimum catch rate. ~10% (Gens 1-4)/~18% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~5% (Gens 1-4)/~10% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 2: "Buffed" minimum catch rate. ~17% (Gens 1-4)/~26% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~9% (Gens 1-4)/~16% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 3: "Super" minimum catch rate. ~27% (Gens 1-4)/~37% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokemon, ~14% (Gens 1-4)/~22% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokemon.
Level 4: "Ultra" minimum catch rate. ~34% (Gens 1-4)/~44% (Gens 5+) chance for all Pokemon. 
Level 5: Guaranteed catches (every Pokemon is guaranteed to be caught, so long as they are catchable in the first place).
wpTRThemedAreasRadioButton:
If this is chosen, every zone will have only Pokemon of a random type.
A "zone" is the area in which a Pokemon will be replaced by the same Pokemon, as determined by the option chosen;
 if the option is "Maximum possible", the zone is instead considered to be a single encounter set (Pokemon encountered in the same place using the same action).
This may lead to a more realistic experience, or an odd one (e.g. if Fire pokemon are chosen to be in Surfing encounters).
wpTRKeepPrimaryTypeRadioButton:
If this is chosen, the random Pokémon that replaces each Pokémon will have the original Pokémon's primary type.
For example, a Grass-Poison Pokémon could be replaced with a pure-Grass Pokémon, a Grass-Psychic Pokémon, or a Bug-Grass Pokémon.
This tends to preserve most type theming, including "soft" type theming like forests having both Bug-type and Grass-type pokemon,
 at the cost of less variance in non-themed areas.
wpTRKeepThemesCheckBox:
If selected, all encounter sets that originally had a type theme (all Pokemon share a type) will keep that type theme.
An encounter set is a set of Pokemon found in the same place at the same time when performing the same action.
It may occasionally have exceptions if the zone has encounter sets with conflicting type themes.
If used with "Random Zone Themes", it will instead override the random theme only if all Pokemon in the whole zone shared a type.
If used with "Keep Primary Type", any theme found will be used instead of the primary type.
tmUnchangedRadioButton:
Leave the moves in TMs as they are.
If Metronome Only Mode is selected, all TMs are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.
tmRandomRadioButton:
Give each TM a new move.
HM moves are not affected, nor can they be selected to be put in TMs.
Each TM will still be unique.
If Metronome Only Mode is selected, all TMs are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.
tmFullHMCompatibilityCheckBox: If you select this option, then every Pokemon will learn every HM, regardless of any other options you check.
tmLevelupMoveSanityCheckBox:
If you select this option, then Pokemon will be guaranteed to learn TMs of moves that they learn by levelup.
Otherwise, move compatibility will be left alone or decided randomly, depending on your other choices.
tmKeepFieldMoveTMsCheckBox:
If you select this, TMs that contain field-use moves will be left alone.
This includes things like Dig & Teleport, but not healing moves (Softboiled).
tmForceGoodDamagingCheckBox:
Selecting this option will allow you to use the slider below to select a proportion of the randomized TMs to be forced to be good damaging moves.
Note that other TMs can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
tmForceGoodDamagingSpinSlider:
Use this slider to select the probability of good damaging moves for the option above.
Note that other TMs can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
tmNoGameBreakingMovesCheckBox:
Checking this checkbox will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized TMs.
In first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.
In second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).
thcUnchangedRadioButton:
Every Pokemon will be able to learn the same TMs that it could before.
Note that this applies even if you change the TM moves, which could lead to some odd combinations.
thcRandomPreferSameTypeRadioButton:
Randomize the TMs and HMs that each Pokemon can learn.
Each TM or HM will have:
A 90% chance of being learnable if the Pokemon has it as (one of) its type(s).
A 50% chance of being learnable if the move is Normal and the Pokemon isn't.
A 25% chance otherwise.
thcRandomCompletelyRadioButton:
Randomize the TMs and HMs that each Pokemon can learn.
Each TM or HM will have a 50% chance of being learnable regardless of type.
thcFullCompatibilityRadioButton:
Select this option to allow every Pokemon to learn every TM/HM.
This can be fun to mess around with, but it might make the game too easy.
mtUnchangedRadioButton:
Leave the moves taught by tutors as they are.
If Metronome Only Mode is selected, all Move Tutors are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.
mtRandomRadioButton:
Give each move tutor slot a new move.
Each Move Tutor move will still be unique, and they will not overlap with TM/HM moves.
If Metronome Only Mode is selected, all Move Tutors are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.
mtLevelupMoveSanityCheckBox:
If you select this option, then Pokemon will be guaranteed to learn move tutors of moves that they learn by levelup.
Otherwise, move compatibility will be left alone or decided randomly, depending on your other choices.
mtKeepFieldMoveTutorsCheckBox:
If you select this, move tutors that contain field-use moves will be left alone.
This includes things like Headbutt, but not healing moves (Softboiled).
mtForceGoodDamagingCheckBox:
Selecting this option will allow you to use the slider below to select a proportion of the randomized tutors to be forced to be good damaging moves.
Note that other tutors can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
mtForceGoodDamagingSpinSlider:
Use this slider to select the probability of good damaging moves for the option above.
Note that other tutors can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
mtNoGameBreakingMovesCheckBox:
Checking this checkbox will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized move tutors.
In first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.
In second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).
mtcUnchangedRadioButton:
Every Pokemon will be able to learn the same move tutor moves that it could before.
Note that this applies even if you randomize the moves, which could lead to some odd combinations.
mtcRandomPreferSameTypeRadioButton:
Randomize the Move Tutor moves that each Pokemon can learn.
Each move will have:
A 90% chance of being learnable if the Pokemon has it as (one of) its type(s).
A 50% chance of being learnable if the move is Normal and the Pokemon isn't.
A 25% chance otherwise.
mtcRandomCompletelyRadioButton:
Randomize the Move Tutor moves that each Pokemon can learn.
Each move will have a 50% chance of being learnable regardless of type.
mtcFullCompatibilityRadioButton:
Select this option to allow every Pokemon to learn every Move Tutor move.
This can be fun to mess around with, but it might make the game too easy.
fiUnchangedRadioButton: Items on the ground and hidden items remain the same.
fiShuffleRadioButton:
Selecting this will take the full set of items that can be picked up from item balls, as well as hidden items,
and randomize their order so each item appears in a new place.
Key items are left in their original location and glitch items are excluded.
This stops item balls containing seriously overpowered items, but more powerful items may be available early on.
TMs will remain in the same item balls, but the numbers of the TMs in them will be shuffled among the set.
fiRandomRadioButton:
Selecting this will place a new random item in each item ball & hidden item slot.
Key items & glitch items are automatically excluded.
This means item balls can contain seriously overpowered items such as Master Balls.
TMs will remain in the same item balls, but the numbers of the TMs in them will be randomized, including TMs not usually available from item balls.
All TMs will still be available at least once in the game.
fiRandomEvenDistributionRadioButton:
This is the same as Random, except that the randomizer will control the number of times each item is placed. 
This applies to the entire game, main- and post-game.
fiBanBadItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for field items, such as berries and mail.
shUnchangedRadioButton: Items in shops remain the same.
shShuffleRadioButton: Items in non-main shops are shuffled.
shRandomRadioButton: Items in non-main shops are randomized.
shBanOverpoweredShopItemsCheckBox:
Checking this will remove overpowered shop items from the pool, such as the Lucky Egg and
items that sell for high prices to maniacs.
shBanBadItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for shop items, such as berries and mail.
shBanRegularShopItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove regular shop items from the possible random items for shop items.
shGuaranteeEvolutionItemsCheckBox: Checking this will ensure all evolution items appear in shops.
shBalanceShopItemPricesCheckBox:
Checking this will change prices for many items in order to make them more balanced.
Be aware: prices for some items are seriously imbalanced without this setting.
shAddRareCandyCheckBox:
Checking this will add cheap Rare Candies to all shops.
(With a few exceptions, such as the HGSS Pokéathlon shops.)
puUnchangedRadioButton: Items obtained via the Pickup ability remain the same.
puRandomRadioButton: Items obtained via the Pickup ability are randomized.
puBanBadItemsCheckBox: Checking this will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for the Pickup item table, such as berries and mail.
miscBWExpPatchCheckBox:
Select this to patch the game you are randomizing to use the Black/White new XP gain system.
This system gives EXP in a different way, rewarding players for beating higher level Pokemon with lower levels.
This is currently available only for English R/B/Y and G/S/C.
miscNerfXAccuracyCheckBox:
X Accuracy in Generation 1 games is a pretty broken item, given that it gives 100% accuracy to any and all moves used.
Apply this code tweak to stop X Accuracy from working on sleep moves, trapping moves & one-hit KO moves.
Doing this means that the player cannot use X Accuracy and lock the opponents into infinite sleep/Wrap, nor can they just use one-hit KO moves on everything.
Applying this patch will also remove the one-hit KO moves from the "broken moves" list if you use that option, since they aren't really broken without X Accuracy.
Credit to Mountebank for this patch.
miscFixCritRateCheckBox:
Selecting this option will "fix" Generation 1's critical hit rate to be the same as the other games (1/16), instead of being based on Speed.
Focus Energy and Dire Hit will also be fixed to increase crit rate instead of decreasing it.
"High crit rate" moves such as Slash will have double the normal crit chance, like in later games.
miscFastestTextCheckBox:
Selecting this option will make all text boxes in the game show up with minimum delay, regardless of the text speed the player sets in Options.
Credit to Revo for Gen 3, Kaphotics for Gen 4, Ajarmar for Gen 5, and unknown cheat code makers for Gen 6/7
miscRunningShoesIndoorsCheckBox: Selecting this option will allow you to use the Running Shoes in any location, just like in later games.
miscRandomizePCPotionCheckBox: Selecting this option will randomize the Potion that is in your item PC at the beginning of the game to any other "useful" item.
miscAllowPikachuEvolutionCheckBox: Selecting this option will let you evolve Pikachu into Raichu with a Thunder Stone like any other game.
miscGiveNationalDexAtCheckBox:
If this is checked then the National Dex will be given to the player at the start of the game with the regular Pokedex.
It is useful for tracking Pokemon outside of the regional dex when using the Pokedex.
Important caveats:
For FRLG only: this setting is necessary for Kanto Pokemon to evolve into Non-Kanto Pokemon, i.e. Golbat evolving into Crobat.
For DPPt only: the National Dex will instead be obtained after speaking to Professor Rowan once after obtaining the regular Pokedex.
forceChallengeMode:
If this is checked, then Challenge Mode will be forcibly enabled, bypassing the Key System entirely.
You will not be able to access Easy or Normal Mode if you enable this setting.
miscLowerCasePokemonNamesCheckBox:
If this is selected, all Pokemon names will be made into Camel Case.
e.g. VENUSAUR becomes Venusaur.
This looks better in Gen3/Gen4 games, and OK in Gen1/Gen2 games.
miscRandomizeCatchingTutorialCheckBox: Selecting this option will randomize the Pokemon participating in the game's catching tutorial.
miscBanLuckyEggCheckBox:
Bans Lucky Egg from showing up as any kind of randomized item.
If the original game contains a Lucky Egg in any non-randomized place, that will still be the case.
miscNoFreeLuckyEggCheckBox: Causes Professor Juniper to not give you a Lucky Egg for free in the Chargestone Cave (BW)/Celestial Tower (BW2).
miscBanBigMoneyManiacCheckBox: Bans maniac items worth more than $10,000 from showing up as any kind of randomized item.
unused8:
This Misc. Tweak should not be visible.
 If you see this, consider making a bug report.
bwPatch:
Select this to patch the game you are randomizing to use the Black/White new XP gain system.
This system gives EXP in a different way, rewarding players for beating higher level Pokemon with lower levels.
This is currently available only for English R/B/Y and G/S/C.
nerfXAcc:
X Accuracy in Generation 1 games is a pretty broken item, given that it gives 100% accuracy to any and all moves used.
Apply this code tweak to stop X Accuracy from working on sleep moves, trapping moves & one-hit KO moves.
Doing this means that the player cannot use X Accuracy and lock the opponents into infinite sleep/Wrap, nor can they just use one-hit KO moves on everything.
Applying this patch will also remove the one-hit KO moves from the "broken moves" list if you use that option, since they aren't really broken without X Accuracy.
Credit to Mountebank for this patch.
critRateFix:
Selecting this option will "fix" Generation 1's critical hit rate to be the same as the other games (1/16), instead of being based on Speed.
Focus Energy and Dire Hit will also be fixed to increase crit rate instead of decreasing it.
"High crit rate" moves such as Slash will have double the normal crit chance, like in later games.
fastestText:
Selecting this option will make all text boxes in the game show up with minimum delay, regardless of the text speed the player sets in Options.
Credit to Revo for Gen 3, Kaphotics for Gen 4, Ajarmar for Gen 5, and unknown cheat code makers for Gen 6/7
runningShoes: Selecting this option will allow you to use the Running Shoes in any location, just like in later games.
pcPotion: Selecting this option will randomize the Potion that is in your item PC at the beginning of the game to any other "useful" item.
pikachuEvo: Selecting this option will let you evolve Pikachu into Raichu with a Thunder Stone like any other game.
nationalDex:
If this is checked then the National Dex will be given to the player at the start of the game with the regular Pokedex.
This is only necessary for FRLG, where certain Pokemon can't evolve if you don't have it.
It is useful in other games for tracking Pokemon outside of the regional dex when using the Pokedex.
typeEffectiveness:
If this is checked, the type weakness/strengths/immunities will be updated to the current set.
For RBY, this means Ghost will be Super Effective against Psychic, among other changes.
lowerCaseNames:
If this is selected, all Pokemon names will be made into Camel Case.
e.g. VENUSAUR becomes Venusaur.
This looks better in Gen3/Gen4 games, and OK in Gen1/Gen2 games.
catchingTutorial: Selecting this option will randomize the Pokemon participating in the game's catching tutorial.
luckyEgg:
Bans Lucky Egg from showing up as any kind of randomized item.
If the original game contains a Lucky Egg in any non-randomized place, that will still be the case.
freeLuckyEgg: Causes Professor Juniper to not give you a Lucky Egg for free in the Chargestone Cave (BW)/Celestial Tower (BW2).
maniacItems: Bans maniac items worth more than $10,000 from showing up as any kind of randomized item.
sosBattles:
Makes it possible for every Pokemon to call allies during wild Pokemon battles.
Without this setting, only Pokemon that could call allies in the base game will be able to call allies.
balanceStaticLevels: Changes levels of Static Pokemon to be more balanced. Currently applies only to fossil Pokemon in FRLG and BW1.
retainAltFormes:
Lets all party Pokemon that are in an alternate forme retain their alternate forme when the game is reset.
Without this setting, Mega Evolutions, Primal Reversions, Ash-Greninja, Zygarde Complete Forme, and Ultra Necrozma will revert to their base forme upon reset.
In ORAS and Gen 7, this setting also prevents certain alternate formes from being reverted after a battle if these formes are not the result of an in-battle transformation.
This includes Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, Wishiwashi School Form, and Minior.
runWithoutRunningShoes: Allows you to run before acquiring the Running Shoes.
fasterHpAndExpBars:
Doubles the scrolling speed of the HP and EXP bars that appear in battle.
In practice, this makes them scroll at the same speed as in the Gen 3 games.
fastDistortionWorld: Cuts out most of the Distortion World by instantly warping you to the Cyrus fight when you enter it.
updateRotomFormeTyping:
Updates the typings of Rotom's alternate formes (i.e., the appliances) to match the typings they have in Gen 5 and onwards.
For example, Wash Rotom will change from Electric/Ghost to Electric/Water.
disableLowHpMusic: Disables the music that plays when one of the player's Pokemon is at low HP in battle, ensuring that the current song will continue playing no matter what.
reusableTMs:
Makes TMs infinitely reusable.
TMs will still act different from HMs in minor ways, such as being tossable/holdable/storable, but their number will never decrease when used.
forgettableHMs:
Makes HMs forgettable like any other move.
Note: If HMs are forgotten in the wrong locations, it is possible to softlock the game.
Be extra careful when releasing Pokémon and (in Gen 1) storing the HM items in your PC.
fastEggHatching: Makes all eggs hatch in as few egg cycles as possible. Generally, this means all eggs will hatch in <256 steps.
noEVYields:
Makes all Pokemon give 0 EVs when defeated in battle.
This does not affect EVs gained using other methods (Vitamins, Power items, Super Training, etc.).
pbsFollowMegaEvosCheckBox:
When this is selected and base stats are shuffled or randomized, Mega Evolutions will inherit from their base form's rolls.
Shuffle: The same new ordering of stats will be used.
Randomized: The Mega Evolution will have the same proportion of stats as the base form.
Not recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.
paFollowMegaEvosCheckBox:
When this is selected and abilities are randomized, non-split Mega Evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit that Pokemon's random abilities.
Not recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.
ptFollowMegaEvosCheckBox:
When this is selected and types are randomized, non-split Mega Evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit that Pokemon's random types (perhaps adding another type).
Not recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.
spAllowAltFormesCheckBox:
Allow alternate formes of Pokemon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Starter Pokemon.
Note that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.
stpAllowAltFormesCheckBox:
Allow alternate formes of Pokemon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Static Pokemon.
Note that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.
stpSwapMegaEvosCheckBox:
Swap Statics capable of Mega Evolution with another Pokemon capable of Mega Evolution.
This affects Lucario in X/Y and Latios/Latias in OR/AS.
tpSwapMegaEvosCheckBox:
Swap Trainer Pokemon capable of Mega Evolution with another Pokemon capable of Mega Evolution.
This only affects Trainer Pokemon that actually hold a Mega Stone (so, for example, it will affect Diantha's Gardevoir but not every Gardevoir)
If the "Limit Pokemon" general option is used to remove all Mega Evolutions from the game, this setting will be disabled.
ptForceDualTypeCheckBox: Checking this will force all Pokemon to have two types when types are randomized
wpAllowAltFormesCheckBox:
Allow alternate formes of Pokemon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Wild Pokemon.
Note that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.
tpBossTrainersCheckBox:
Check this to add additional Pokemon to "Boss" Trainers (select amount of new Pokemon below). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokemon.
Boss Trainers include Gym Leaders, Kahunas, Team Leaders, Elite Four, and Champions.
tpImportantTrainersCheckBox:
Check this to add additional Pokemon to "Important" Trainers (select amount of new Pokemon below). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokemon.
Important Trainers include Rivals/Friends, Team Admins, and other important story battles (such as Colress in BW2 and Sycamore in XY).
tpRegularTrainersCheckBox:
Check this to add additional Pokemon to regular Trainers (select amount of new Pokemon below). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokemon.
Regular Trainers include all trainers that don't qualify as "Boss" or "Important" Trainers.
peAllowAltFormesCheckBox: Allow Pokemon to evolve into alternate formes of Pokemon, including into regional variants.
tpRandomShinyTrainerPokemonCheckBox: Gives a 1/256 chance of Trainer Pokemon being shiny.
totpAuraRandomSameStrengthRadioButton:
Auras will be randomized to auras with the same net gain of stages.
For example, a Totem Pokemon that previously had +2 Speed could get +2 Defense instead.
Totem Pokemon with +1/+2 to every stat will not have their auras randomized, since those auras are the only ones with 5 and 10 stages respectively.
totpRandomSimilarStrengthRadioButton: Replace every Totem Pokemon with a Pokemon of similar strength.
totpAllyRandomSimilarStrengthRadioButton: Replace Ally Pokemon with Pokemon of similar strength.
totpRandomizeHeldItemsCheckBox: Replace Totem Pokemon's held items with different consumable items.
totpAllowAltFormesCheckBox: Allows alternate formes of Pokemon to appear as Totem/Ally Pokemon.
totpPercentageLevelModifierCheckBox: Checking this will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every Totem/Ally Pokemon.
pmsEvolutionMovesCheckBox:
Selecting this option will cause every Pokemon to learn a move upon evolution.
Use carefully with Sun/Moon 1.0 - due to a glitch, if a Pokemon has an evolution move and also learns a move
on the level that it evolved at, it will only learn the evolution move upon evolving.
paWeighDuplicatesTogetherCheckBox:
This setting causes abilities that have the exact same effect to be considered as the same ability for randomization probability purposes. Every variation of the respective abilities can still appear.
This applies to:
Gen 3+: Insomnia/Vital Spirit, Clear Body/White Smoke, Huge Power/Pure Power, Battle Armor/Shell Armor, Cloud Nine/Air Lock
Gen 4+: Filter/Solid Rock
Gen 5+: Rough Skin/Iron Barbs, Mold Breaker/Turboblaze/Teravolt
Gen 7+: Wimp Out/Emergency Exit, Queenly Majesty/Dazzling, Gooey/Tangling Hair, Receiver/Power of Alchemy, Clear Body/White Smoke/Full Metal Body, Multiscale/Shadow Shield, Filter/Solid Rock/Prism Armor
tmFollowEvolutionsCheckBox:
When this is selected and TM compatibility is randomized, evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit that Pokemon's TM compatibilities.
Additionally, when a Pokemon evolves, each TM will have:
Random (prefer same type): A 90% chance of becoming learnable if the Pokemon just gained its type through evolution, a 10% chance otherwise.
Random (completely): A 25% chance of becoming learnable regardless of type.
mtFollowEvolutionsCheckBox:
When this is selected and move tutor compatibility is randomized, evolutions of a Pokemon will inherit that Pokemon's move tutor compatibilities.
Additionally, when a Pokemon evolves, each move will have:
Random (prefer same type): A 90% chance of becoming learnable if the Pokemon just gained its type through evolution, a 10% chance otherwise.
Random (completely): A 25% chance of becoming learnable regardless of type.
stpFixMusicAllCheckBox:
Fixes the music for all Static Pokemon encounters so that even when randomized, encounters that should have special music will play the correct song.
Note that in Gen 4/5, if special music is assigned to a Pokemon then it will always play when battling that Pokemon, even if you just find it normally in the wild.
tpBossTrainersItemsCheckBox:
Check this to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of "Boss" Trainers.
Boss Trainers include Gym Leaders, Kahunas, Team Leaders, Elite Four, and Champions.
tpImportantTrainersItemsCheckBox:
Check this to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of "Important" Trainers.
Important Trainers include Rivals/Friends, Team Admins, and other important story battles (such as Colress in BW2 and Sycamore in XY).
tpRegularTrainersItemsCheckBox:
Check this to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of regular Trainers.
Regular Trainers include all trainers that don't qualify as "Boss" or "Important" Trainers.
tpBossTrainersTypeDiversityCheckBox:
Check this to ensure that "Boss" trainers do not use multiple Pokémon of the same type.
If the trainer has a type theme, this option will be ignored.
If 'Additional Pokemon for Boss Trainers' is selected but Trainer Pokemon are 'Unchanged', only the added Pokemon are guaranteed diverse types.
Boss Trainers include Gym Leaders, Kahunas, Team Leaders, Elite Four, and Champions.
tpImportantTrainersTypeDiversityCheckBox:
Check this to ensure that "Important" trainers do not use multiple Pokémon of the same type.
If the trainer has a type theme, this option will be ignored.
If 'Additional Pokemon for Important Trainers' is selected but Trainer Pokemon are 'Unchanged', only the added Pokemon are guaranteed diverse types.
Important Trainers include Rivals/Friends, Team Admins, and other important story battles (such as Colress in BW2 and Sycamore in XY).
tpRegularTrainersTypeDiversityCheckBox:
Check this to ensure that regular trainers do not use multiple Pokémon of the same type.
If the trainer has a type theme, this option will be ignored.
If 'Additional Pokemon for Regular Trainers' is selected but Trainer Pokemon are 'Unchanged', only the added Pokemon are guaranteed diverse types.
Regular Trainers include all trainers that don't qualify as "Boss" or "Important" Trainers.
tpEliteFourUniquePokemonCheckBox:
Enabling this setting will ensure that Pokemon League Trainers (Elite Four, Champions and BW1 N/Ghetsis) 
are given the specified number of unique Pokemon that will not appear on any other Trainer.
The Elite Four Trainers' highest level Pokemon are the ones that will be unique;
in the case of a level tie, it will be the Pokemon further back in the party.
Does not apply to postgame Pokemon League battles.
tpBetterMovesetsBossTrainersCheckBox:
Check this to give "Boss" trainers better movesets by including TM moves/tutor moves/egg moves/pre-evolution moves,
and picking moves that synergize with the Pokemon's ability/stats/other moves.
tpBetterMovesetsImportantTrainersCheckBo:
Check this to give "Important" trainers better movesets by including TM moves/tutor moves/egg moves/pre-evolution moves,
and picking moves that synergize with the Pokemon's ability/stats/other moves.
tpBetterMovesetsRegularTrainersCheckBox:
Check this to give regular trainers better movesets by including TM moves/tutor moves/egg moves/pre-evolution moves,
and picking moves that synergize with the Pokemon's ability/stats/other moves.
ppalRandomRadioButton: Selecting this will give each Pokemon a random color palette.
ppalFollowTypesCheckBox:
When this is selected, Pokémon colors will depend on type. 
 For example, a Fire-type Bulbasaur might be red, and a Grass-type Groudon might be green.
ppalFollowEvolutionsCheckBox:
When this is selected, each Pokémon species will have colors similar to those it evolves to/from.
When evolutions are randomized, Pokémon get colors similar to their new evolutions/prevolutions.
If "Follow Types" is selected, a Pokémon that gets a new type upon evolution may have its colors reflecting this.
ppalShinyFromNormalCheckBox: When this is selected, the shiny colors of each Pokémon species becomes the colors it would normally have, if palettes were not randomized.
cpgCustomRadioButton: Player graphics are replaced by custom ones, chosen here in the randomizer.
cpgReplaceLabel: Choose which character to use custom graphics for.
tpUseLocalPokemon:
Trainers use only Pokemon that can be found in the wild and their evolutionary relatives.
If used with "Pokemon League has Unique Pokemon", those Pokemon are instead chosen from the set of non-local Pokemon.
spTypeTriangleRadioButton:
Chooses any three types that form a triangle of super-effective attacks.
Does not guarantee resistances in the other direction.
If allowing dual types, does not guarantee that second types will not break the triangle.
spRandomBasicRadioButton:
Picks 3 random starter Pokemon to be used.
These Pokemon must not be evolved forms of any other Pokemon, but they may or may not evolve.
spTypeNoDualCheckBox:
Guarantees that the Pokemon chosen will not be dual-types.
They may still evolve into dual-types.
spTypeSingleRadioButton:
All randomly-chosen starters will be of the selected type.
 If set to "Random", a single type will be chosen and all randomly-chosen starters will be of that type.
 Warning: This setting may cause the randomization to fail when used with others restricting which Pokemon may be chosen, due to a lack of Pokemon fulfilling the criteria.
 E.g. choosing "Random (basic Pokemon with 2 evolutions)" and "Fighting" as the type will cause a failed randomization in
 all generations, as Machop and Timburr are the only basic Fighting Pokemon with 2 evolutions. And earlier generations have the same issues with many other types.
 "Random (any basic Pokemon)", "No Dual Types", "No Legandaries" etc. may also cause failures.
 When Pokemon types are not randomized, it is possible for the user to figure out which combination of options may work or not
 (e.g. in Gen 1, there will never be any non-dual type Ghost Pokemon, and Gen 4 is the first generation with 3 basic non-legendary Dragon Pokémon). 
 If Pokemon types are randomized, failing is more purely probabilistic. As a rule, later generations have more Pokémon and are thus less likely to fail.
spTypeUniqueRadioButton: Randomly-chosen starters will not share types with others in their trio.
teRandomBalancedRadioButton: Like Random, but ensures no Type has more weaknesses/resistances/immunities, offensively and defensively, than any Type in the base game.
teKeepTypeIdentitiesRadioButton:
Type Effectiveness is randomized, but Types keep their number of weaknesses/resistances/immunities, offensively and defensively.
 E.g. Normal Types will be weak to 1 Type, immune to 1, be resisted by 2 (or 1 in Gen 1), and have 1 Type be immune to them.
teInverseRadioButton:
All weaknesses become resistances, and all resistances and immunities become weaknesses, like the Inverse Battles of Gen 6.
 E.g. Fire type moves become super effective against Water Pokémon, but not very effective against Grass Types.
teAddRandomImmunitiesCheckBox:
If selected, a few weaknesses will become immunities instead of weaknesses.
 E.g. Grass Types might become immune to Fire Type attacks, instead of just resisting them.
 The number of immunities added are the same as in the base game (6 in Gen 1, 7 in Gens 2-5, 8 in Gen 6+).
teUpdateTypeEffectivenessCheckBox:
If selected, the type weaknesses/resistances/immunities will be updated to what they are in Gen 6 and up.
This is done before any randomization.
This does NOT add the Fairy type.
For Gen 1, this changes the following:
• Ice is now not very effective against Fire.
• Poison is now neutral against Bug.
• Bug is now not very effective against Poison.
• Ghost is now super effective against Psychic.For Gens 2-5, this changes the following:
• Ghost is now neutral against Steel.
• Dark is now neutral against Steel.
peForceGrowthCheckBox: When this is checked, random evolutions will always have a higher BST than the Pokemon they evolve from.
peNoConvergenceCheckBox: When this is checked, no two Pokemon will evolve into the same Pokemon.
spBstLimitsLabel:
If the boxes below are checked, will choose starters that have above the minimum and/or below the maximum base stats entered.
For reference, all starter Pokemon (excepting Pikachu and Eevee) in vanilla games are in the stat range 307-320 (249-253 in Generation 1).
spBSTMinimumCheckbox:
If checked, no Pokemon will be chosen as a starter if it has a base stat total lower than the number below (they can have the same).
For reference, the lowest base stat total any starter (except Pikachu) in the base games has is 307 (249 in Gen 1).
spBSTMinimumSpinner:
The lowest base stat total a chosen starter may have (inclusive).
For reference, the lowest base stat total any starter (except Pikachu) in the base games has is 307 (249 in Gen 1).
spBSTMaximumCheckbox:
If checked, no Pokemon will be chosen as a starter if it has a base stat total higher than the number below.
For reference, the highest BST any starter (excluding Eevee) in the base games has is 320 (253 in Generation 1).
spBSTMaximumSpinner:
The highest base stat total a chosen starter may have (inclusive).
For reference, the highest BST any starter (excluding Eevee) in the base games has is 320 (253 in Generation 1).
tpUnchangedBattleStyleRadioButton: Don't change the Trainer's battle style at all.
tpRandomBattleStyleRadioButton:
Sets all Trainer battles to a random battle style instead of single battles. The first rival battle is excluded.
Other trainers with only one Pokemon will have that Pokemon duplicated.
Be aware that there are a few issues with this. In particular:
• Entering a multi-battle with not enough pokemon causes some generation-dependent issues:
• Gen 3: The empty spot will be filled by a duplicate of the single Pokemon, and entering the "Pok?mon" menu will softlock the game.
• Gen 4: The empty spot will be filled by a garbled sprite that only can use Struggle.
• Gen 6/7: The empty spot will be filled by a shiny Bulbasaur that cannot act.
• In Gen 5 games, Trainer pairs that are double battles in the regular game will have one incorrect text box if you let them spot you.
• In Gen 6 games, regular Trainers will have some text issues if you talk to them directly.
tpSingleStyleBattleStyleRadioButton:
Change all Trainer Battle Styles to the selected style. The first rival battle is excluded.
Other trainers with only one Pokemon will have that Pokemon duplicated.
Be aware that there are a few issues with this. In particular:
• Entering a multi-battle with not enough pokemon causes some generation-dependent issues:
• Gen 3: The empty spot will be filled by a duplicate of the single Pokemon, and entering the "Pok?mon" menu will softlock the game.
• Gen 4: The empty spot will be filled by a garbled sprite that only can use Struggle.
• Gen 6/7: The empty spot will be filled by a shiny Bulbasaur that cannot act.
• In Gen 5 games, Trainer pairs that are double battles in the regular game will have one incorrect text box if you let them spot you.
• In Gen 6 games, regular Trainers will have some text issues if you talk to them directly.
tpBattleStyle1Single: Sets all Trainer battles to be single battles.
tpBattleStyle2Double: Sets all Trainer battles to be double battles.
tpBattleStyle3Triple: Sets all Trainer battles to be triple battles.
tpBattleStyle4Rotation: Sets all Trainer battles to be rotation battles.
pbstUnchangedRadioButton: Pokemon Base Stat Totals are not changed.
pbstRandomBuffNerfRadioButton:
Each Pokemon recieves a random buff or nerf to their BST.
The slider below decides the maximum BST change, in percentages.
(If set to 20, a Pokemon will randomly get between 80-120% of their original BST)
pbstShuffleRadioButton:
Shuffle the BSTs of all Pokemon.
If there were originally 6 Pokémon with 600 BST, there will be 6 after applying this option,
but the Pokémon will be different.
E.g., Weedle might receive the BST of Mewtwo, Charizard the BST of Butterfree.
pbstRandomRadioButton: Each Pokemon gets a completely random BST.
pbstFollowEvolutionsCheckBox:
If used with "Random Buff/Nerf (%)", each Pokemon in a family will get the same buff/nerf.
If used with "Shuffle", BSTs will be shuffled family-by-family, going by length.
(3-stage families will be shuffled with 3-stage families, 2-stage families with 2-stage families,
non-evolving mons with non-evolving mons)
pbstSwapLegendariesCheckBox:
If selected, legendary Pokemon will have their BSTs shuffled separately from all other Pokemon.
This prevents extremes like Mewtwo getting the BST of Farfetch'd, and vice versa,
while still allowing variation within each category.
